answers.explanation: The passage implies one naira meals exist at the Sports Club, so the claim that nowhere sells food for one naira is not implied.
Obi says the gate men check for something that looks like an identity card, so entry requires one.
Obi says V.I.Ps do not wear badges and that you must pose to get along, so only those who can pose break queues.
Obi says there are many impostors and many people with privileges, so many people claim privileges in Nigeria.
Obi and Olu accept posing and privilege-seeking as normal, which makes them typical of Nigerian society.
A bolus is a lump or mouthful of food, which is closest to a large morsel.
The passage says they hardly noticed the sun come up and go down, so they hardly noticed the land turning brown.
The passage says Teresa gave the children only bits and reserved the whole chunk of meat for her husband.
Ntanya thanks Teresa after eating, and she is the one who serves him, so he addresses his wife as mother.
By claiming she had already eaten, Teresa leaves the food for Ntanya, who eats to his satisfaction.
The passage is the author's own argument that mathematics is an art, so the views are the author's.
Calling mathematics the queen of the sciences compares it to a queen, which is an analogy.
Capital M marks Mathematics as a subject or field, distinguishing it from the concept used in the passage.
The sentence is phrased as a question, but the writer uses it to state his own conclusion.
The passage says mathematics, like art, involves a study of beauty, harmony and order.
The senator denies receiving any of the N50,000 fund and clears himself of the charges against him.
A constituent is a person with voting rights in the area where he lives.
Accosted here means approached and spoken to, which is closest to went and spoke to.
The senator says every kobo of the N50,000 has been used to defray political campaign expenses.
The passage sends Tony Agiwa to Abu O. Abu for details of the fund, and records are kept by the Administrator, so Abu is the fund's administrator.
The family's hopes ran high because the goats had started producing milk, which they poured on their porridge.
The adults ignored the children's scolding of their rag-dolls, which is what this sentence refers to.
The family sat in despair because it was impossible to plant corn, maize and other seeds in the dry earth.
The passage says the animals were sold during the bad years to purchase food.
The children imitate their mothers in running a home, scolding and beating the rag-dolls as adults do.

Indifferent means uninterested, so its opposite is interested in.
Severity means harshness, so its opposite is mildness.
Deterred means discouraged, so its opposite is encouraged.
To entitle someone is to give them a right, so its opposite is to disqualify.
An abridged edition is shortened, so its opposite is enlarged.
Being afraid of his own shadow means he is timid, which is closest to scared of imaginary things.
Knocking your head against a brick wall means attempting something impossible.
To have a chip on one's shoulder means to be easily angered or resentful.
To become popular means to be welcomed and accepted by others.
To take exception to a remark means to object to it.
Hardly ever falling sick means very seldom.
To meet one's Waterloo means to suffer a decisive defeat.
Futile means useless or pointless, which is closest to vain.
To be knocked out means to be made unconscious.
Incessantly means without stopping, which is closest to continuously.
Marvellous condition means excellent condition.
To maintain good humour means to keep it, which is closest to kept.
Democracy is government by the people, so the closest option is government by all the people.
Momentarily means for a brief period of time.
Willy nilly means whether one wants it or not, so he was compelled to leave.
The penultimate paragraph is the last but one.
A hindrance is an obstacle to development.
A door left ajar is left open.
If people break the rules, the passage means they will have themselves to blame.
Predominantly means mainly.
Punitive laws are severe penalties, so punitive is closest to severe.
Indefinitely means without a fixed date.
A laissez-faire attitude is relaxed and careless.
To cope with tasks means to manage them.
Unmitigated means complete and absolute, which is closest to unqualified.
To be above board means to be honest, which is closest to above suspicion.
Foolhardiness is reckless risk-taking, which is closest to foolish risk-taking.
To be given to much wine means to be addicted to it.
To be taken in by someone means to be deceived by them.
To come to grips with oneself means to master one's difficulties.
To come down heavily on someone means to impose a stiff penalty.
Witch-hunting and character assassination mean accusing people unjustly and maliciously.
White elephant projects are costly projects of little use.
Going to school by bus means using the bus as the means of travel.
To stare at someone is to look at them, which takes the preposition at.
Unrest results in something, which takes the preposition in.
To insist on something means to demand it, which takes on.
Children are afraid of thunder, which takes of.
To rush to a place is the correct phrase, which takes to.
To be taken in by lies is to be deceived by them.
To be sorry for failing to attend is the correct gerund form, for failing.
To keep one's mind on the job is the correct idiom, which takes on.
The reported clause after a past verb takes the past form, so what he wanted.
I'm working describes an action in progress at the moment on the farm.
An action completed before another past event takes the past perfect, had started writing.
The enthusiasm was waning, a continuing past state, so was waning fits.
To value the initial worth of the hotel complex at ten million naira is the sense of the sentence, so had valued fits.
James needs reminding, a common construction with needs as an intransitive verb in the passive sense.
A means to an end takes the infinitive to improve.
Not any more dangerous than riding a bicycle uses the phrase not any more.
Do not want any advice is the correct form, since no or not is not used with no double negative.
Satisfactory accommodation is the correct spelling.
To cash in on something means to profit from it, which fits exploiting the people's ignorance.
A plane overshoots the runway, the strip used for take-off and landing.
Occurrence is the correct spelling.
To run out of luck means to lose good fortune.
The thief was robbing the passengers, the correct verb for the action.
To desist from rumour-mongering takes the preposition from.
Damage is uncountable in this sense, so damage to my car is correct.
Information is uncountable, so no plural or article is used.
The possessive pronoun Ngozi's stands alone for Ngozi's script.
A pat on the back takes the preposition on.
